_comment: Add this to your Claude Desktop configuration to run the CimPal MCP server from the Docker image instead of the JAR. See docs/cli/docker.md.
_how_to_use: Merge the 'mcpServers' block into your existing claude_desktop_config.json. Replace C:/Data with the folder that holds your models, shapes and outputs. Docker Desktop must be running.

cimpal._note_args: '-i' keeps stdin open for the MCP stdio channel; never add '-t'. '-v C:/Data:/data' mounts your folder at /data, and every path in a tool call must then be a container path such as /data/models. Pin a release instead of 'latest' for reproducible results, e.g. ghcr.io/griddigit-ci/cimpal:2026.10.1.1.
cimpal._note_mounts: Safer: mount inputs read-only and give the tools a separate writable output folder, e.g. "-v", "C:/Data/models:/data/models:ro", "-v", "C:/Data/out:/data/out".
cimpal._note_token: For remote owl:imports with a GitHub token, add "-e", "GITHUB_TOKEN" to args (no value, before the image name) and put the value in an "env": {"GITHUB_TOKEN": "..."} block of this server. Never write the value into args, where any process listing shows it.
cimpal._note_memory: For large CGMES models, set the heap before the image name: ["run", "-i", "--rm", "-e", "JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx8g", ...]. Docker Desktop's VM memory is the upper bound. Never put secrets in JAVA_OPTS: it shows in docker inspect.
cimpal._note_debug: To see MCP message traffic, add '--debug' after 'mcp'. Debug output goes to stderr, not the MCP channel.
